title: Reserved GPU Credit Brokerage — strategy and model sketch
content:
Purpose
This is a working sketch for a "credit brokerage" overlay on top of our Reserved GPU / commit model. Idea: allow flexible transfer/matching of unused reserved capacity across a negotiated market-like mechanism so we reduce idle sunk cost, preserve predictable revenue, and offer customers lower effective rates when they accept pooled or laddered commitments.

Context / Pain
- Large reserved purchases are stickier but create utilization cliffs and idle sinks at tail months.
- Sales/CS frequently negotiate bespoke commits; engineering needs a predictable reservation demand signal.
- We can reduce overall gross margin loss from underutilized pools by enabling intra-pool reallocation, temporary brokerage of credits, and priced burst-topups that sit between dedicated and hosted.

Objectives
1) Reduce idle-reservation waste by 20–40% across mid-sized contracts (10–200 GPUs).
2) Keep effective price to customers transparent and bounded (no surprise overages).
3) Maintain minimum committed revenue for finance while enabling secondary consumption.

High-level mechanics (sketch)
- Commit Token: 1 token = 1 reserved GPU-hour at a baseline commit rate. Customers buy tokens monthly or upfront for a period.
- Brokerage Pool: Unused tokens from enrolled contracts are pooled into a regional market for a discounted consumption by other enrolled customers or for our own short-term burst-to-hosted layer.
- Settlement: Weekly/day-end accounting of token transfers, with automated refunds or credits applied to owner contracts. Owner contracts retain base SLA except when tokens are leased out under explicit rules (opt-in by contract).
- Pricing bands: Brokered usage priced at a tiered discount relative to on-demand and below hosted list price but above marginal cost recovered by hosting/spot.

Risk controls and opt-ins
- Customer opt-in required for each contract and scoped by region, GPU family, and time windows.
- Hard floor: we cannot broker tokens that would violate contract-level SLA minima (e.g., pinned capacity during business hours).
- Audit trail: transfers logged per token with timestamp, region, and consuming identity for billing and compliance.

Suggested spreadsheet (tab map + column sketch)
Tab: contracts_master
Columns: contract_id | customer | region | gpu_family | commit_gpus | commit_hours_per_month | unit_monthly_rate | opt_in_flag | blackout_windows | owner_margin_target

Tab: utilization_daily_feed
Columns: date | region | gpu_family | contract_id | reserved_hours_available | reserved_hours_used | unused_hours | spot_backfill_hours | hosted_fallback_hours

Tab: brokerage_ledger (core)
Columns: day | token_id | from_contract | to_contract_or_hosted | hours_transferred | price_per_hour | fee_pct | settlement_amount | note
Sample row: 2025-02-25 | token-95 | CUST-204 | HOSTED-BURST | 12 | $3.25 | 5% | $37.05 | weekly settlement

Tab: scenario_analysis (what this doc focuses on)
Columns: scenario_name | enrolled_pool_size_gpus | avg_util_pct_pre | expected_idle_hours | brokered_hours | spot_mix_pct | effective_unit_cost_reserved ($/gpu-hour) | effective_unit_cost_brokered | blended_unit_cost | breakeven_months_vs-hosted
Sample calculations (spreadsheet formulas in plain text)
- expected_idle_hours = commit_gpus * hours_in_month * (1 - avg_util_pct_pre)
- brokered_hours = min(expected_idle_hours, enrolled_pool_spare_capacity * participation_factor)
- effective_unit_cost_reserved = unit_monthly_rate / hours_in_month
- effective_unit_cost_brokered = (unit_monthly_rate * lease_rate_share + spot_hourly_cost * spot_mix_pct) / (1 + leakage_adj)
- blended_unit_cost = ((used_reserved_hours * effective_unit_cost_reserved) + (brokered_hours * effective_unit_cost_brokered) + (spot_backfill_hours * spot_hourly_cost)) / total_consumed_hours

Concrete mini-scenarios (quick numbers to sanity check)
- Baseline: 50 GPUs reserved region-east, unit_monthly_rate = $5,000/GPU-month -> hours_in_month = 730 -> reserved_unit_hour = $6.85/hour. Average utilization pre-broker: 70% -> idle_hours = 50*730*0.30 = 10,950h.
- If we broker 30% of idle (3,285h) at brokerage price $3.50/h + 5% fee to platform: settlement roughly $12k/month extra recovered vs $0 if idle. That reduces effective blended cost by ~8–12% for owner contract assuming owner reduces list price by negotiated share.

Metrics to report in dashboard (console integration)
- Pool utilization rate (by region/gpu_family)
- Revenue recaptured from brokerage (MTD, QoQ)
- Owner contract effective discount & realized unit cost
- Churn correlation (opt-in vs renewed)
- SLA breach incidents caused by brokered transfers (should be near 0)

Operational considerations
- Billing: weekly settlement reduces surprise; show line-item in invoice as "Brokerage credit/usage". Finance needs a gross-to-net mapping for revenue recognition.
- Engineering: small routing shim at schedulers to mark capacity reserved vs brokered; KV used for blackout windows.
- Legal: T&Cs update, opt-in consent, data residency for cross-customer transfers in regions with restrictions.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should we allow customer-to-customer direct sublease (marketplace) or keep platform acting as counterparty? (Tradeoff: legal + complexity vs margin)
- What percentage fee is acceptable (benchmark: 5–15%)? Run sensitivity on owner realized saving vs platform take.
- How to model long-tail churn if brokers consistently capture cheaper customers leading to sticky hosted usage?

Quick next steps (for this WIP)
1) Build a lightweight Google Sheet with the tabs above and pipe in 6 months of anonymized utilization for 20 mid-size contracts. (Owner: Ethan, due 2025-02-20)
2) Run sensitivity sweeps on: broker_fee_pct = [3,5,10], participation_factor = [0.2,0.5,0.8], spot_mix_pct = [0.1,0.3]. (Owner: Marta, due 2025-02-27)
3) Legal draft for opt-in clause and blackout constraints. (Owner: Daniel, due 2025-03-07)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a product/finance hybrid sketch — not final pricing. Focus feedback on governance (who can opt-in), settlement cadence, and what protections we must bake into SLAs.
- If we pursue this, prioritize a safe, conservative pilot (one region, one GPU family, limited customer cohort).

Appendix: quick list of spreadsheet column sanity checks
- Ensure hours_in_month normalized (use 720 for planning, 730 for true months; pick one and stick to it across sheets).
- Use consistent GPU family naming (a100-40, a100-80, h100-v2) to avoid misapplied transfers.
- Tag blackout windows in ISO intervals to allow accurate overlap checks before transfer.

End of sketch — feedback welcome.
